a.lean.let.roundtrip.moved: The pinned GAP was a text-PARSE refusal (roundtrip:text-parse:fn-name): the producer's entity names leave the bare-identifier alphabet (`m::dep_clamp`, `m::Pt<u8>`), and text had no spelling for them, so the module did not survive `bin -> text -> bin` at all. trust-ir now prints `@"escaped"` and `Parser::read_name` decodes it (WS4.3 identifier half), which closes the PARSE half. Reaching PASS also needed the TRANSPORT to stop canonicalizing: `trust-ir convert --to text` encoded through `format::canonical_checked`, which renumbers SSA values densely and reorders blocks before printing — a DECLARED rewrite that `text_losses` deliberately does not report, so a non-canonical module came back re-numbered with an EMPTY loss list. trust-ir bef296c7 adds `format::text_checked` (same refusal, module printed AS STORED) and points `convert` at it. MEASURED on this tree, as a control over the 24 producer-emitted modules this lane compiles: 10 of the 24 are NOT canonical, and `bin -> text -> bin` is byte-identical for 24/24 with `text_checked` but only 14/24 with canonicalize-first. So both halves were required and neither alone would have flipped this pin.
